ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2017; real-time screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, FATF Public Statements (black and grey lists), Australian DFAT Consolidated List, and Vanuatu domestic sanctions administered by the Vanuatu FIU; enhanced due diligence requiring original government-issued ID, independent source of funds/worth verification, and senior management approval for any PEP, or any individual or entity connected to a sanctioned jurisdiction, deal must be refused and report filed with the Financial Intelligence Unit within 5 business days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Online Name Reservation and e-Registry Portal via registered agents; official registry: VFSC Companies Office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in English or French; where a foreign name is used, it must be transliterated into the English alphabet; an International Company must not have a name that is identical or deceptively similar to a name already reserved or registered in Vanuatu; the name must include a legal element such as 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', or 'Ltd' unless exempted by the VFSC; the official script for registration records is Roman script (English/French transliteration).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registered agent may submit a written request for reconsideration to the VFSC within 14 days of the notice of rejection; the request must state the grounds for review and include the original proposed name reservation number and any supporting evidence of entitlement to use the sensitive token; if the name is rejected due to similarity with an existing entity, the appellant may identify a distinguishing element or obtain a letter of non-objection from the existing copyright/trademark owner; if the VFSC upholds the rejection, the applicant may apply to the Supreme Court of Vanuatu for judicial review under the Judicature Act Cap. 60 and Rules of Court; a fresh reservation application may be filed with a 30-day new validity period. Filing of the appeal before the VFSC must be made through a VFSC-licensed registered agent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in Vanuatu is mandatory; the registered agent may provide a virtual office accommodating mail forwarding and director/UBO communication channels; however, the International Company must maintain a physical address in Vanuatu for service of process. For the online jewelry/watch e-commerce trade through Stripe and PayPal, a virtual office accepted by payment intermediaries is permissible, but the VFSC and Vanuatu FIU expect a documented physical place of business or contractual commercial representative in Vanuatu for substance documentation; a pure virtual office is accepted for initial incorporation but may be rejected by acquiring banks or payment processors during merchant underwriting.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-high risk at 35-50% within the first 12 months; VFSC and the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit conduct unannounced on-site inspections under Section 29 of the AML/CFT Act 2017 where a company is engaged in e-commerce sectors interfacing with multiple foreign payment rails; sector risk rating of Medium_Risk_Enhanced for ISIC 4791 increases the probability of documentary and physical compliance inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap 222] of the Republic of Vanuatu (Act No. 32 of 1992, as amended) - incorporation under Part II, registered office and registered agent administrative provisions, and the section 132 taxation exemption.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division, Port Vila, Vanuatu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Prescribed Application for Registration of an International Company (VFSC Form IC-1) filed together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; the memorandum may declare an authorized capital of a single no-par-value share, with consideration satisfied by cash, promissory note, or other lawful value.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the application for incorporation of the Company as an International Company under the International Companies Act [Cap 222] be approved and that the subscribing incorporator be and is hereby ratified in delivering the Memorandum and Articles of Association to the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission. FURTHER RESOLVED that the allotment of the initial subscribed ordinary shares to the founding subscriber be confirmed and recorded in the share register. FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office and registered agent be designated at Port Vila, Vanuatu. FURTHER RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed first Director and that the Director be authorized to open bank and payment-account relationships and to execute all operational contracts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage VFSC-licensed registered agent and clear corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), International Companies Registry, acting through a VFSC-licensed Registered Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed registered agent to submit a name-clearance request to the VFSC Registry. The proposed name must include 'Limited', 'Ltd.', or an approved abbreviation, must be distinguishable from existing registered names, and must not contain wording implying Crown patronage or prohibited activity. Secure written name availability before executing constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Name clearance request form
Letter of engagement with the licensed registered agent
Identity details of the proposed subscriber
Proposed name and two alternative names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, promptly resubmit with alternative names within two business days; no application fee is forfeited if only the name is queried.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles in VFSC-prescribed form, specifying no-par-value or par-value shares, objects limited to lawful offshore business, registered agent clauses, and indemnity provisions. The subscriber executes the documents; signatures of foreign subscribers must be witnessed or notarized, with certified passport and proof of address attached.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber declaration and consent
Notarized/certified passport copy of subscriber and proposed director
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
Power of attorney in favor of the registered agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any factual discrepancies (name spelling, director details) and re-execute the documents; post-registration amendments to the Memorandum and Articles may also be effected under the IC Act amendment provisions without re-facing VFSC rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File registration application with the VFSC
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges the prescribed application (Form IC-1) with the executed Memorandum and Articles, declarations, registered agent consent, and payment of the prescribed government fee. The VFSC performs a statutory compliance review and, upon approval, issues the certificate under the Commission's seal.
required_dossiers: VFSC Form IC-1 (Application for Registration of an International Company)
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent's consent and declaration
Subscriber's statutory declaration
Consent of the registered office provider
Government fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any VFSC query within 14 calendar days; where the application documents are defective, withdraw and refile corrected documents; a late cure at this stage attracts no penalty beyond the initial fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and VFSC corporate file extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry Division.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the registration number and date of incorporation, together with the sealed copy of the Memorandum and Articles. Verify the company name, legal existence, and registry particulars, and obtain certified copies of the certificate for banking and payment-processor onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Sealed/registered Memorandum and Articles of Association
VFSC corporate file extract
Register of Directors, Secretary and Members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical errors, request correction from the VFSC within a reasonable period; a duplicate certificate is obtainable upon payment of the prescribed VFSC fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convene first board meeting and complete governance formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board, recorded by the registered agent in the Vanuatu corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution confirming share subscription and allotment, appointing the first Director and any corporate officers, adopting the registered office and registered agent, approving the corporate seal and share certificates, and authorizing opening of bank and payment accounts.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution minutes
Share certificate and share register ledger
Register of Directors and Secretaries
Register of Members
Signed consents to act of each director and officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer appointment is corrected or changed, file the statutory change notice with the VFSC within 21 days to avoid administrative late-filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain tax-exempt confirmation and payment-account onboarding package
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) and the licensed registered agent; downstream banks and payment processors separately.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirmation of the automatic exemption from Vanuatu income tax, stamp duty, and exchange control under section 132 of the IC Act. Procure a VFSC Certificate of Good Standing and certified incorporation package for Stripe/PayPal due diligence, including beneficial ownership declaration under the AML/CFT regime.
required_dossiers: VFSC Certificate of Good Standing
Certified true copy of Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of registered Memorandum and Articles
Beneficial ownership register and declaration
Director and shareholder identity documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VFSC queries beneficial ownership filings, update the register and submit the revised declaration within the statutory deadline; where a Good Standing certificate has lapsed, reapply and pay the required fee for a fresh certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Department of Industry, Ministry of Trade, Tourism, Industry and Cooperatives, Port Vila - applicable only where a domestic business licence would be triggered; domestic trading is prohibited for International Companies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for offshore online merchandising of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces; a Business Licence under the Business Licence Act [Cap 35] would only apply to a separate domestic entity carrying on trading activities within Vanuatu.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation, Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology, Geo-Hazards, Energy, Environment and National Disaster Management.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category C; online retail distribution and small-parcel logistics generate no scheduled activity under the Environment Act No. 12 of 2002, so no EIA registration or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC point-source emissions; general municipal solid-waste disposal rules apply to packaging and returned goods; lithium-ion watch batteries must be transported under UN3481 in accordance with IATA Packing Instruction 966/967 and are not subject to Basel transboundary movement control at retail parcel volumes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance from the Vanuatu Police Force - Fire Service for any leased office or secure storage premises; structural load certification by a licensed engineer for jewelry vault shelving or high-density racking under the applicable national building code; workplace health and safe-handling protocols per Vanuatu occupational health and safety regulations; no hazardous-process clearance required for retail jewelry and watch operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR) — administrative contact via the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) for International Company registration and licensing; no separate national income-tax portal exists because Vanuatu levies no direct taxation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Vanuatu International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act [Cap 222] is registered with VFSC and receives a Certificate of Incorporation bearing a unique company number that serves as its national identifier; no VAT/TIN number is issued. The IC must file an annual return with VFSC but is not required to register with DCIR for income-tax purposes. If the IC physically imports goods into Vanuatu, it must separately obtain a Customs Importer Code from DCIR under the Customs Act [Cap 195].
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Vanuatu imposes no corporate income tax; there is no check-the-box regime, no tax treaty network, and no hybrid-mismatch or fiscal-transparency election available. An IC is statutorily exempt from all present and future Vanuatu taxes on income, profits, distributions, and capital gains (International Companies Act, s.129).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not_Applicable_as_a_VAT_concept. Vanuatu does not levy VAT, GST, exporter sales tax, or any zero-rated export mechanism. Exports of jewelry, watches, and fashion merchandise are outside any indirect tax charge; no refund claim is possible or required. Physical exports leaving Vanuatu are subject only to customs export clearance formalities, with no ad valorem export duty on finished jewelry or timepieces.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (approved form under the Customs Act [Cap 195])
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (to evidence the external sale for anti-money-laundering and VFSC recordkeeping, given Stripe/PayPal settlement flows)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback is applicable because no indirect tax on exports exists. However, penalties apply for misuse of IC status: an International Company engaging in prohibited domestic business with Vanuatu residents, or carrying on business without maintaining a registered agent, forfeits its statutory tax exemption and is liable under the International Companies Act [Cap 222] to fines of up to VUV 500,000. False customs export declarations are prosecuted under the Customs Act [Cap 195] with confiscation of goods, monetary penalties, and imprisonment on conviction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), established under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act (Cap. 125); the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) is the non-bank financial services regulator but the RBV retains prudential regulation of banking and foreign exchange.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu has no exchange controls and maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility. The legal tender is the Vanuatu Vatu (VUV), but foreign currency accounts are freely permitted. There are no profit-repatriation hurdles, no withholding taxes on dividends of an International Company, no exchange control licences, and no requirement for government permission for outward capital flows. For an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act (Cap. 259), remittance of capital, dividends, loan repayments, and trade payments can be executed freely; banking partners will nonetheless apply ordinary anti-money-laundering (AML) and know-your-client (KYC) filters to verify source of wealth, transaction purpose, and absence of sanctioned parties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Vanuatu imposes no statutory export-receipt surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in any currency in local or foreign bank accounts, used directly for trade settlement, or repatriated without central bank notification. The only applicable requirement is standard reporting by banks to the RBV for macro-prudential statistics and suspicious-transaction reporting under the AML/CFT Act, not individual trade-flow approval.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility, with important legal constraints. Vanuatu does not issue a distinct 'Electronic Money Institution' license. A non-bank accepting customer moneys or executing payment transactions must hold a banking license under the Banking Act (Cap. 63) or be registered as a Financial Dealer under the Financial Dealers Act (Cap. 60) and be regulated by the VFSC/RBV. Offshore digital EMIs licensed in the EU, UK, Australia, or Singapore may service the Vanuatu entity from abroad and provide accessible multi-currency settlement, but they generally cannot open local VUV clearing accounts without an RBV-approved bank acting as agent. For this e-commerce jewelry/watch operation, global PSP rails (Stripe, PayPal) are commercially permitted for customer collections, but the core operating liquidity, supplier disbursement, and capital escrow should remain in a tier-1 Vanuatu financial institution to reduce settlement and regulatory risk.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Vanuatu law does not impose a blanket statutory requirement for directors to appear physically. Under the RBV's AML/CFT CDD directives, account onboarding is risk-based; in practice tier-1 banks permit hybrid/remote onboarding for International Companies: certified passport copies, apostilled constitutional documents, board resolutions, certificate of incumbency, source-of-wealth statements, and a live video KYC interview. ANZ and Bred Bank are more likely to accept this no-face-to-face model for non-resident directors; BSP and NBV may require an override or a local director/registered agent with authorization to meet the bank. A local registered agent is not mandatory for the bank account itself, but materially improves onboarding speed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner is a non-resident, offshore-domiciled individual with no prior Vanuatu bank relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle consisting of a current passport (notarized and apostilled), a board resolution authorising account opening, a certificate of incumbency from the registered agent, a VFSC extract of the International Company, a source-of-wealth statement supported by audited accounts or regulated-bank statements, and an official regulatory reference letter from any existing foreign regulated bank showing no adverse history.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value goods (fine jewelry and timepieces) triggering enhanced due diligence due to elevated money-laundering typology risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial documentation: product catalogue with photos and serial numbers (for timepieces), supplier invoices, dealer resale/consignment agreements, transport and insurance certificates, and a written AML/PEP/sanctions compliance policy for the e-commerce platform. Add a client-risk assessment matrix and a copy-calculation showing that average transaction values and volumes are consistent with ordinary online luxury trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection originated from a non-regulated vehicle or aggregated payment-service-provider account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a structured source-of-funds chain: equity declaration, audited financial statements or accountancy report, a notarized letter from the beneficial owner describing the funds, and bank statements from the original remitting regulated account. Confirm that no client funds from the Stripe/PayPal settlement are commingled before the capital injection; arrange a direct remittance from an ordinary regulated bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound wire transfers to suppliers in high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., China, UAE, Hong Kong) or to finance vendors that manufacture replicas/counterfeit goods.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver commercial purchase orders, supply agreements, letters of credit, shipping bill of lading or air waybill, inward invoice matching, and the supplier's own business license and directorship list. Include a screenshot of the supplier's online presence and the eBay/Amazon store registration link for the e-commerce affiliate model. Provide transaction narrative in the SWIFT field 72 showing the goods description and the unique invoice number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cross-border FX conversions at inconsistent rates or unusual use of third-party intermediary currencies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Create and maintain a treasury cadence showing purchase/settlement currency needs; provide invoices denominated in USD/EUR/CAD/AUD; attach FX rate confirmations, and clearly state that no pass-through financing or third-party payment arrangement exists. If a local third party attempts to settle on behalf of the company, the bank will require a foreign-exchange service-provider agreement and ensure the beneficiary name remains the final commercial supplier.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Vanuatu International Company, inbound equity capital is accepted through SWIFT MT103 from the beneficial owner's regulated bank account or, for larger rounds, via MT202COV where the intermediary bank needs cover. Use the BPM6/ISO 20022 purpose code B011 for contributed equity capital (or B013 for intercompany loan); in the SWIFT remittance information field (FT 72) state 'Share Capital Contribution / Loan per Facility Agreement'. Route the wire through established correspondents (ANZ Melbourne/Sydney, Bred Bank's Paris/Luxembourg correspondent, or BSP Asia Pacific) to avoid intermediary fees. The bank will verify the beneficiary name exactly as it appears on the VFSC registration; no RBV approval or foreign-investor permit is required for an International Company. Retain a copy of the board resolution and shareholder register for the capital injection for the customer-due-diligence file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments for jewelry and watch inventory should be cleared primarily by SWIFT MT103 straight-through transfers for orders under USD 100,000, and by confirmed irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT710) for larger consignments or when supplier terms demand documentary security. For recurring procurements from Hong Kong, Singapore, UAE, and India, use a designated beneficiary name exactly matching the invoice; include the purchase order number, invoice reference, and goods classification in the SWIFT narrative. For LCs, a senior domestic bank can issue on the basis of the client's credit or cash collateral; this provides supplier-side confidence without earlier payment at risk. Cross-currency settlement is free of exchange-control restrictions; the account bank may quote VUV/USD for televised transfers, but it is advisable to retain USD/EUR/AUD clearing lines to reduce two-step conversion exposure. For outbound PayPal/Stripe remittances to the Vanuatu operational account, settlement occurs in USD/EUR/AUD and requires linking to a regulated bank account; all PSP settlement funds must be traceable to the original customer sale to satisfy AML audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts: Vanuatu-licensed ADI banks may write deliverable forwards on VUV/USD, AUD/USD, EUR/USD, and GBP/USD to lock trade settlement rates, provided there is an underlying commercial transaction and the bank does not take an uncovered speculative position.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): permitted on currencies with restricted onshore convertibility (e.g., CNY, INR, PHP, KRW, IDR, and AED/AED-related pairs) through international counterparties; NDF cash settlement is executed in USD, not in VUV, and is subject to standard ISDA/IFX master agreements.

Cross-Currency Swaps: vanilla interest rate and principal swaps between VUV, USD, AUD, and EUR are available through treasury teams of major internationally-licensed banks where the Vanuatu entity maintains a global-liquidity account; these are permissible when used to convert foreign-currency funding or hedge balance-sheet risk, but must be documented under an ISDA agreement with a qualified-rated counterparty to avoid regulatory re-characterization as a speculative exchange contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Renewal Filing (International Company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; annual return and renewal fee are due on the anniversary date each year, with a grace period before late penalties accrue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-fee surcharge of 25% of the applicable annual fee; continued non-filing for more than 12 months exposes the company to administrative strike-off from the register; restoration requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and a restoration fee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Update and Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual return on the anniversary of incorporation; share transfers changing the ultimate beneficial owner must be recorded promptly and reflected in the next annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Bundled with the annual return at no additional government charge; failure to maintain and update the beneficial ownership register may lead to rejection of the annual return and penalties under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2019

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a standard International Company under the International Companies Act Cap. 222; independently audited financial statements are required only for regulated licensees (banking, insurance, securities); a retail e-commerce merchant holding no VFSC licence has no statutory audit obligation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No local GAAP mandate; financial records may be prepared under IFRS on a voluntary basis for banking, investor, or payment processor due-diligence purposes

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each International Company must maintain a register of beneficial owners under the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2019; share transfers that change the ultimate beneficial owner are recorded in the register and confirmed to VFSC through the annual return process, which operates as the annual UBO confirmation event

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit required; voluntary audit USD 1,500–4,000 per annum for a small e-commerce entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (nil) — Vanuatu levies no national corporate income tax; an International Company is statutorily exempt from all income, profit, and capital-gains taxes under the tax-exemption provisions of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222].
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Automatic zero-rate status for every registered IC regardless of industry; no capital gains tax, no payroll tax, no net wealth tax, and no tax on distributions. Qualifying offshore e-commerce receipts are outside the scope of the 12.5% Value Added Tax [Cap. 247]. The only mandatory annual charges are the VFSC government fee (approximately VUV 45,000) and the registered agent's professional fee.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return exists in Vanuatu. The mandatory equivalent is the VFSC Annual Return, submitted electronically by a licensed registered agent through the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) online registry portal, together with remittance of the annual government fee.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 4 months after each anniversary of incorporation; the annual government fee is payable at the same time. Failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registrar of International Companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered legal name, IC registration number, date of incorporation, and company status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State details exactly as registered. No Vanuatu tax identification number is required because no income tax exists; a non-resident beneficial owner may insert the home-country fiscal number where the registered agent requires it for CDD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B — Registered Office and Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Vanuatu and the identity of the VFSC-licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A real physical address in Vanuatu is compulsory; a P.O. box alone is insufficient. The licensed agent must be retained continuously, and any change of agent or office must be notified within 30 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal names, residential addresses, nationality, and identification documents of all directors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors are expressly permitted; 100% foreign management is lawful. The registered agent must hold certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each director.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D — Shareholders and Beneficial Owners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Register of members (names, addresses, class and number of shares) plus the separately maintained beneficial-ownership register filed with the VFSC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: 100% non-resident ownership is allowed. Bearer shares are prohibited. Nominee arrangements must be disclosed to the agent, and the ultimate beneficial owner must be entered in the VFSC beneficial-ownership database.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification that the IC has not carried on local business in Vanuatu, holds no Vanuatu land or immovable property, and has contravened no provision of the International Companies Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an e-commerce IC, certify that all sales via Stripe and PayPal were concluded outside Vanuatu, no customers were Vanuatu residents, and no inventory, employees, or fulfillment operations were located in Vanuatu.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual self-assessment of any relevant activity (e.g., distribution and service centre, holding entity) and confirmation of substance indicators maintained in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure offshore reseller with no office, staff, or expenditure in Vanuatu must not falsely claim substance. If no relevant activity is conducted in Vanuatu, state this expressly; a false declaration attracts the economic-substance penalty regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late lodgement penalty of approximately VUV 10,000 per commenced month, capped at VUV 50,000 per year; continuing default leads to administrative strike-off and dissolution, after which assets escheat and bank/payment-processor accounts are frozen. Officers of the company may additionally be fined up to VUV 100,000 under the International Companies Act for non-compliance with the annual-return filing obligation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — dividends paid by a Vanuatu International Company to resident or non-resident shareholders are wholly exempt from Vanuatu withholding tax. No dividend declaration duty, no gross-up, and no exchange-control approval is required for outward remittance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu has no comprehensive double-tax treaty network. Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) are in force with Australia, New Zealand, Greenland, and the Nordic states; a Vanuatu–UAE DTA has also been signed and domestically approved. Because the domestic withholding rate is already nil, no treaty-relief application is required. A shareholder seeking a foreign-tax-credit in its residence state obtains a Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency from the VFSC through the registered agent; this document substitutes for a Tax Residency Certificate and evidences the IC's zero-tax status.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory and effective rate on both interest and royalties paid by an IC to non-residents. No domestic obligation to report, withhold, or declare such payments to Vanuatu authorities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Vanuatu transfer-pricing statute or domestic documentation threshold exists. Market practice under OECD standards: prepare contemporaneous local-file-equivalent documentation when annual related-party transactions exceed VUV 10,000,000 (approximately USD 83,000); full master file plus country-by-country reporting readiness is prudent when group turnover approaches EUR 750,000,000 due to OECD Inclusive Framework GloBE rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic-substance requirements apply under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act 2022/2023, implementing EU and OECD/G20 commitments. An IC conducting a relevant activity, including 'distribution and service centre' (e-commerce sales, logistics, procurement) or 'holding entity' business, must demonstrate in Vanuatu: (1) direction and management (board meetings held in Vanuatu); (2) adequate physical premises; (3) full-time qualified employees; (4) adequate annual operating expenditure. A jewelry-and-watches e-commerce IC that operates as a Stripe/PayPal shell with substance located elsewhere is in breach. Penalties reach VUV 10,000,000, with deregistration and information exchange to the beneficial owner's jurisdiction as consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Offshore Tax Evasion and Permanent Establishment Exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting the real e-commerce business (contracting, marketing, inventory, management) from a high-tax country while invoking the Vanuatu zero-tax exemption without registering or filing in the market country; creating a permanent establishment through home-office directors or third-party fulfillment centers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu side: VFSC strike-off and fines up to VUV 100,000 for false declarations. Foreign side: full tax reassessment with penalties (up to 75% accuracy-related penalty in the United States; up to 100% base penalty in Australia), VAT/GST back-claims, and enforcement against the company's bank accounts and payment-processor balances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face director penalty notices in Australia and analogous personal-liability regimes elsewhere, making them personally liable for unpaid company taxes. Criminal tax-evasion convictions carry imprisonment (United States: up to 5 years per count under 26 U.S.C. § 7201; Australia: up to 10 years under Criminal Code s 134.2), alongside travel bans, extradition, and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC with no staff, office, or management in Vanuatu; claiming a relevant activity such as a distribution and service centre without substance; failing to file the annual economic-substance declaration; using the IC merely to hold Stripe/PayPal rails for an owner-managed foreign business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Economic-substance financial penalty up to VUV 10,000,000; daily default fines; compulsory deregistration with asset forfeiture; adverse referral through TIEA channels to the beneficial owner's tax authority, triggering CFC and foreign-entity-classification rules that eliminate the zero-tax benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are jointly and severally liable for ESR civil penalties and may be disqualified from acting as directors. Beneficial owners face reclassification of the entity as a shell under EU ATAD Annex V rules, resulting in tax-residence reallocation and look-through taxation in their country of tax residence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / CFT and Payment-Rails Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting high-value payments for watches or jewelry without customer due diligence or source-of-wealth verification; processing tip-off or third-party funds; transacting in non-KYC cryptoassets; concealing beneficial ownership; dealing in counterfeit luxury brands or conflict diamonds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu AML/CFT Act No. 21 of 2016: civil penalties up to VUV 20,000,000 for reporting-entity failures; money-laundering penalties under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2005 include imprisonment up to 20 years; VFSC suspension of the registered agent; Stripe and PayPal permanent account termination, rolling-reserve confiscation, and referral to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers knowingly involved face personal fines up to VUV 5,000,000 and imprisonment for money-laundering offences. Directors may be named in global AML enforcement actions, triggering Interpol red notices, extradition requests, and civil asset-recovery orders extending to personal and family property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent Trading, False Declarations, and Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors knowingly signing VFSC annual returns that falsely state 'no operations' while the online jewelry business actively trades; continuing to trade while insolvent to defraud creditors; misrepresenting the IC's zero-tax status to foreign revenue authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Officer-level fines up to VUV 100,000 under the International Companies Act; fraudulent-trading provisions of the Companies Act [Cap. 191] render the wrongdoer personally liable without limitation; the Supreme Court may order winding up, confiscation, and disqualification of directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for all company debts to creditors and revenue authorities; criminal fraud prosecution under the Penal Code [Cap. 135] may result in imprisonment, confiscation orders, a 10-year directorship ban, and a travel ban imposed by the Supreme Court of Vanuatu.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding customer prepayments or escrow deposits for high-value watch transactions, earning float on client funds, or acting as an unlicensed payment intermediary for third-party sellers — all without a VFSC money-services or dealer license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Carrying on regulated financial business without a VFSC license is a criminal offence punishable by fines up to VUV 10,000,000 and imprisonment; the Supreme Court may wind up the company and order restitution of client funds; affected contracts are void and unenforceable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are criminally liable for unlicensed financial-services activity and are jointly and severally ordered to repay customer funds personally; continued operation after a VFSC cease-and-desist notice results in custodial sentences and asset-freezing orders.
